pooled.note: Observed = distinct stocked products per invoice; simulated = distinct items per visit. 14,776 of 19,773 invoices hold at least one of the 72 products placed in the shop; the rest are left out.

Observed = one unit of each stocked product on an invoice, at the shop's calibrated prices; simulated = one unit of each item a visit bought. 14,776 of 19,773 invoices hold at least one of the 72 products placed in the shop; the rest are left out.

Whole baskets: 14,776 invoices holding at least one of the 72 products placed in the shop against 1,815 simulated visits that bought one, each reduced to its purchases of those products per category (9 categories; 68,005 reference and 8,436 simulated purchases). Statistic = Pearson chi-square of the 2 x K table of category totals; p from 2,000 random reassignments of the visit / invoice labels (seed 20260924), which move each basket whole. Naive item-level p = 0.00046 (the chi-square(8) tail, which treats every purchase as independent; the reassigned statistics average 1.50 x its null mean).

Informational: tests whether the dataset's inter-arrival times are approximately Poisson (the family the simulator assumes), against a reference stamped at the source's 60 s resolution. The reference rate is constant, while the data's rate (and the simulator's) varies by hour of day, so a rejection can come from that variation too.
